Finish setup with your agent.

FluxVale org: your organization (<your-org-slug>)
API base: http://localhost:4000
MCP server: https://mcp.fluxvale.com/mcp

Auth: Mint a scoped token at http://localhost:4000/settings/developer#api-tokens with scopes catalog:read, instances:write, wallet:read, export it as `FLUXVALE_PAT`, and send it as `Authorization: Bearer $FLUXVALE_PAT` on the MCP connection. A client that speaks OAuth will open a browser sign-in instead once OAuth ships.

You are my FluxVale setup agent. Connect to the MCP server above, then:
1. Call `whoami`, then `wallet_balance`. If the balance is zero or negative, stop and give me the top-up link: http://localhost:4000/billing/topup. Do not deploy.
2. Ask what I want to run, then pick an app from `apps_list` and call `apps_show`: it lists versions with the default CPU, memory, and storage and a `monthly_cents` rate. Propose one version and that price (billed hourly).
3. Confirm the spend with me before deploying. Never deploy without an explicit yes.
4. Deploy with `instances_deploy`. Put configuration in `env`, for example {"TZ":"UTC"}. Leave cpu/memory/storage off to take the version's defaults.
5. Poll `instances_status` until it is running, then give me the row's `url` — that is the instance URL.
6. Change env later with `instances_configure`: `set` adds or replaces, `remove` deletes. Values are write-only — never print them.
7. Never run `instances_destroy` or `backups_restore` without a separate, explicit yes.
8. After the app runs, offer Terraform if I want to manage it as code: http://localhost:4000/docs/automation/terraform.

Reference: http://localhost:4000/docs/agents
